clues: the user updated the wireless adapter software yesterday
a blue stop error screen appears soon after sign-in
the stop error comes back on every restart
the PC starts normally in Safe Mode

answer.cause: the newly installed wireless adapter driver is faulty
answer.action: Boot into Safe Mode and roll back the wireless adapter driver in Device Manager

firstStep: Note the stop code and the driver file named on the blue screen
appliesWhen: a stop error began right after a device driver was updated
explanation: A new or corrupt driver is a common cause of a stop error, and Safe Mode loads only basic drivers so Windows can start. Rolling back the driver returns the device to the version that worked.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

clues: the stop errors started after more memory was added
each blue screen shows a different stop code
the crashes happen at random times, even in Safe Mode
no drivers or updates were installed recently

answer.cause: a new memory module is not seated correctly or is faulty
answer.action: Reseat the new memory modules and test the RAM with a memory diagnostic

appliesWhen: random stop errors started after a memory upgrade
explanation: Improperly seated or faulty RAM causes random stop errors with changing codes, even when only basic drivers load. Reseating and testing the memory confirms the fault.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

clues: every application is slow to respond
the case fan runs much louder than usual
the Task Manager Performance tab shows the processor near 100 percent
memory and disk use are normal

answer.cause: one process is using almost all of the processor time
answer.action: Find the process on the Processes tab, then end it or move its work to a quieter time

appliesWhen: one busy process is holding the processor at full load
explanation: Task Manager shows which of the CPU, memory, disk, network, and GPU areas is overloaded. Sorting the Processes tab by CPU shows the process that causes the load.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the drive activity light stays on almost all the time
switching between open programs is very slow
the user keeps a database, a browser, and email open all day
the processor is not busy when the slowdown happens

answer.cause: the PC does not have enough RAM, so Windows keeps paging memory to the drive
answer.action: Add more RAM to the computer

firstStep: Check memory use on the Task Manager Performance tab
appliesWhen: the PC runs out of physical memory under its normal workload
explanation: When physical memory runs out, Windows swaps less active memory pages to the page file on the drive. That causes heavy drive activity and slow programs, so more RAM is the lasting fix.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: a low memory warning appears after the PC has run for several hours
the warning does not appear right after a restart
one program's memory use keeps growing on the Processes tab
the PC has the amount of RAM the vendor recommends

answer.cause: one program is using much more memory than it normally needs
answer.action: End the program, then update or repair it so it stops using so much memory

appliesWhen: a single process keeps taking more memory than it should
explanation: A low memory warning means Windows cannot page out any more memory. When one process keeps growing on a PC with enough RAM, that process is the problem, not the hardware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: low memory warnings started after a user changed the virtual memory settings
the page file is now set to a few hundred megabytes
programs close without warning when several are open
the drive has plenty of free space

answer.cause: the page file was set too small
answer.action: Set the page file back to a system-managed size in the Virtual Memory settings

appliesWhen: the page file was made too small for the workload
explanation: Windows moves idle memory pages to the page file, so a page file that is too small causes low memory warnings and instability. Letting Windows manage the size, or making it at least 1.5 times the RAM, fixes it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the power failed while the PC was installing updates
the PC now stops with a boot error before the sign-in screen
the recovery environment opens after two failed starts
the drive passes the firmware's hardware test

answer.cause: the boot configuration data that the boot manager reads is damaged
answer.action: Run Startup Repair from the Windows Recovery Environment

appliesWhen: Windows cannot start because its boot files are damaged but the drive works
explanation: The boot manager reads the BCD to find and load Windows, so a damaged BCD stops the boot. Startup Repair in WinRE rebuilds the boot data, much like bootrec /rebuildbcd.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the user copied files from a flash drive before restarting
the screen says no operating system was found
the drive is listed in the firmware setup
the same PC booted normally that morning

answer.cause: the firmware tries to boot from the flash drive left in a USB port
answer.action: Remove the flash drive and set the firmware to boot from the internal drive first

firstStep: Check the USB ports and optical drive for media
appliesWhen: removable media is left in the PC and the firmware boots from it first
explanation: When removable media comes before the internal drive in the boot order, the firmware tries to boot from it and finds no OS. Putting the internal drive first prevents the problem and closes a security gap.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

clues: the screen says no operating system was found
the internal drive is not listed in the firmware setup
no media is attached and the boot order is correct
the PC was moved to a new desk yesterday

answer.cause: the system drive is disconnected or has failed
answer.action: Reseat the drive's data and power cables, and replace the drive if the firmware still cannot see it

appliesWhen: the firmware cannot detect the system drive at all
explanation: If the firmware cannot see the drive, no repair tool in Windows can help, because WinRE also starts from that drive. Checking the cables comes first, then replacing a failed drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

clues: the PC turns off when nobody has used it for a while
the System log shows a normal shutdown entry from the kernel each time
it never turns off while someone is working on it
no hardware or drivers were changed

answer.cause: the power plan puts the PC to sleep or turns it off after a short idle time
answer.action: Change the sleep and power settings in Power Options so the PC stays on when plugged in

appliesWhen: Windows itself is turning the PC off because of its power settings
explanation: Kernel entries in the System log show whether Windows shut down on purpose or lost power. A normal shutdown while idle points to the power settings, not to hardware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the PC turns off suddenly with no warning
it happens most often when the PC is under heavy load
the System log shows unexpected shutdowns with no normal shutdown entry
the user hears no change in the fans before it turns off

answer.cause: the power supply is failing and cuts power to the PC
answer.action: Test the power supply and swap in a known good unit

firstStep: Check the System log in Event Viewer for how the PC shut down
appliesWhen: the PC loses power suddenly instead of shutting down through Windows
explanation: When the log shows a dirty shutdown with no kernel shutdown entry, the PC lost power rather than Windows turning itself off. Intermittent power loss is often caused by the power supply or other failing hardware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

clues: a backup service does not start when Windows starts
the System log shows event ID 7000 with a logon failure
the service account's password was reset last week
the service worked until then

answer.cause: the service still uses the old password of its logon account
answer.action: Enter the account's current password on the Log On tab of the service's properties

firstStep: Check the System log in Event Viewer for the service's error
appliesWhen: a service fails because its logon account details are wrong
explanation: A logon failure in event 7000 from the Service Control Manager points to the account the service runs as. The password on the Log On tab must match the account, and the account must not be locked out.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: a service stopped starting after a new application was installed
the System log shows event ID 7000 for the service
the error does not mention a logon failure
the service's logon account is correct

answer.cause: the new application conflicts with resources the service needs
answer.action: Reinstall the software that installed the failing service

appliesWhen: a service fails after other software claimed the resources it needs
explanation: A service that fails without a logon error is often in conflict with another program's resources. Reinstalling the service's software is the quickest way to restore what it needs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: a program crashes as soon as it opens
the problem began after a different program was installed
an error names a missing DLL file
other programs on the PC work normally

answer.cause: the program's critical files were overwritten or corrupted
answer.action: Repair the program from the Advanced options in Installed apps

appliesWhen: one program's own installed files are missing or damaged
explanation: Another installer can overwrite a program's DLL files. A repair checks the installation and replaces the critical files without touching data or settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the design program crashes when large drawings are opened
the crashes started after the program was upgraded to a new version
the PC has less RAM and video memory than the new version requires
a repair of the program did not help

answer.cause: the PC does not meet the new version's hardware requirements
answer.action: Add RAM and a graphics card that meet the vendor's requirements

appliesWhen: the hardware is below what the program's vendor requires
explanation: Each program needs a certain amount of RAM, storage, CPU speed, and sometimes GPU memory. If the PC falls below the vendor's requirements, the hardware must be scaled up.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: a warning says there are not enough USB controller resources
a keyboard, a mouse, a webcam, and three drives use the fast ports
the last device connected does not work
each device works when connected alone

answer.cause: too many devices on the USB 3.0 controller use up its endpoints
answer.action: Move the keyboard and mouse to USB 2.0 ports and keep only fast devices on USB 3.0

appliesWhen: too many devices on one controller use up its data endpoints
explanation: Each USB controller has a fixed number of endpoints for data. Moving slow devices such as keyboards and mice to the other controller frees endpoints for the devices that need speed.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: several devices are connected through one unpowered hub
the devices disconnect at random
the problem gets worse when an external drive spins up
each device works when connected straight to the PC

answer.cause: the devices draw more power than the hub's port can supply
answer.action: Connect the devices through a powered hub or spread them across more ports

appliesWhen: the connected devices need more power than the port supplies
explanation: A USB port can supply only a limited current, for example 500 mA for USB 2.0 and 900 mA for USB 3.0. A device that draws more than its share malfunctions or disconnects.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: several programs began crashing on the same day
the PC installed Windows updates the night before
the PC sometimes freezes and has to be restarted
no new hardware or programs were added

answer.cause: a recent Windows update is causing the instability
answer.action: Uninstall the recent update from Update history

firstStep: Check Reliability Monitor for the day the crashes began
appliesWhen: the problems began right after an update was installed
explanation: Reliability Monitor shows crashes and installed updates on the same timeline. When the trouble starts right after an update, removing that update returns the system to its stable state.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: signing in to the domain takes about five minutes
signing in with a local account takes seconds
the user stores gigabytes of downloads in the profile
sign-out is also slow

answer.cause: the large roaming profile has to be copied across the network at each sign-in and sign-out
answer.action: Delete temporary and downloaded files to shrink the roaming profile

appliesWhen: a bloated roaming profile is copied from the server at sign-in
explanation: A roaming profile loads from a server at sign-in and is written back at sign-out. Removing temporary Internet files and downloads makes it much smaller, so it loads faster.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

clues: the desktop takes several minutes to become usable after sign-in
many icons appear in the notification area during that time
the user signs in with a local account
the PC runs normally once sign-in has finished

answer.cause: too many programs are set to start when the profile loads
answer.action: Disable unneeded startup apps on the Startup tab of Task Manager

appliesWhen: programs set to start at sign-in slow down a local profile
explanation: Items that start with the profile can slow a local sign-in. Disabling them in Task Manager one by one, with test sign-ins, shows which ones cause the delay.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the PC's clock is several minutes behind
sign-ins to the domain fail with an error
websites show certificate errors
the firewall was recently changed to block more outbound traffic

answer.cause: the PC cannot reach its time server, so the clock has drifted
answer.action: Allow the PC to reach the NTP server and sync the clock in Date & time settings

firstStep: Select Sync now in Date & time settings and read the result
appliesWhen: the clock has drifted because the PC cannot reach a time server
explanation: Windows corrects the real-time clock by querying an NTP server, so blocking the server lets the clock drift. A large drift breaks domain sign-in and makes certificates look invalid.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

clues: the clock drifts a few minutes each day
the system runs as a virtual machine on a server
the host server's clock is correct
the guest tools were never installed

answer.cause: the virtual machine's emulated clock is not synced to the host
answer.action: Install the hypervisor's guest tools or integration services so the guest syncs its clock to the host

appliesWhen: a virtual machine's clock is not synced with its host
explanation: A hypervisor emulates the real-time clock, so a guest's clock drifts much more than a physical PC's. The guest tools sync the guest clock to the host, which syncs with an NTP server.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

need: return Windows system settings and drivers to the state they were in last week
clues: system protection was turned on before the trouble began
the problems started after several programs and drivers were installed
the user's documents must stay as they are
appliesWhen: Windows must go back to an earlier restore point without touching personal files
explanation: System Restore returns system files, settings, and drivers to a restore point. It keeps personal files, but it removes programs, updates, and drivers added after that point.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

need: see on a daily timeline which programs crashed and which updates were installed
clues: a program has crashed now and then for a month
the user cannot remember when the trouble began
the technician wants to compare the crash dates with update dates
appliesWhen: crashes and updates must be compared on a timeline
explanation: Reliability Monitor draws a stability graph and lists program crashes, Windows failures, and updates by date. That shows what changed just before the problems began.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

need: see live disk and network activity for each process in more detail than Task Manager
clues: the Task Manager view shows heavy disk use but not which files are involved
the PC slows down during the afternoon
the technician wants to filter the activity for one process
appliesWhen: detailed live performance data for each process is needed
explanation: Resource Monitor shows real-time CPU, memory, disk, and network data for every process. Selecting a process filters the other views to show only that process's activity.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

need: start Windows with all third-party services turned off to see if one of them causes the problem
clues: the PC shuts down at random
the problem started after several programs were installed
the technician wants to test without deleting any software
appliesWhen: Windows must start with a selective set of services or startup items
explanation: On the Services tab of MSConfig, the technician can hide all Microsoft services and disable the rest, then restart and test. Normal startup must be restored afterward.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

need: find out why a service failed to start this morning
clues: the service is set to start automatically
no error message appeared on the screen
the technician wants the error ID and its description
appliesWhen: the logged reason for a failure must be found
explanation: The Service Control Manager writes event ID 7000 to the System log when a service fails to start. The event description gives the reason, for example a logon failure.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

need: check and replace damaged protected Windows files
clues: several Windows features have started to show errors
the technician suspects file corruption
the PC still starts to the desktop
appliesWhen: protected system files may be corrupt while Windows still runs
explanation: The System File Checker scans the protected Windows files and replaces any that fail the integrity check. It can also run offline from WinRE when Windows cannot start.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

need: reinstall Windows but keep the user's personal files
clues: file checks and repairs did not fix the errors
no restore points exist
the company does not use a standard image

answer.item: Reset this PC with Keep my files

appliesWhen: Windows must be reinstalled in place while the user's files are kept
explanation: Reset this PC reinstalls Windows from a cloud download or a local copy. The Keep my files choice keeps the user's data, while Remove everything wipes it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

need: return a broken PC to the company's standard build as fast as possible
clues: the company keeps a standard image with all programs preinstalled
reinstalling each program by hand would take hours
the user's files are kept on a server

answer.item: Reimaging the PC with System Image Recovery

appliesWhen: a prepared system image exists and is faster than reinstalling software
explanation: When reinstalling software would take longer than restoring a prepared image, reimaging is the fastest fix. System Image Recovery in WinRE reloads the operating system and programs from the image.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

need: give one user a clean sign-in without the clutter that slows it down
clues: only this user's sign-in is slow on the PC
deleting temporary files did not help
the user's documents must be kept

answer.item: Rebuilding the user profile after backing up its files

appliesWhen: one user's own profile is damaged or bloated
explanation: Deleting the profile in the User Profiles settings lets Windows build a new one at the next sign-in. Copy the profile folder first, then copy the user's files back.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

need: make a service start again by itself when it stops unexpectedly
clues: the service crashes about once a week
nobody is there to start it by hand at night
the vendor has not released a fix yet

answer.item: Setting restart actions on the Recovery tab of the service's properties

appliesWhen: a service must restart by itself after a failure
explanation: The Recovery tab sets what happens on the first, second, and later failures of a service. It can restart the service, run a program, or restart the computer.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

need: fix a crashing program while keeping its data and settings
clues: the program crashes on start
its files may have been overwritten by another installer
the user does not want to set it up again

answer.item: Repairing the program from Installed apps

appliesWhen: one program's own files must be checked and replaced
explanation: A repair checks the program's installation and replaces missing critical files such as DLLs. It leaves data and configuration files untouched.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the notes app shows only a blank screen when it is tapped
the app was used earlier in the day and then swiped away
other apps open normally
the app worked yesterday

answer.cause: the app is still hung in the background and only comes to the foreground
answer.action: Force stop the app and open it again

appliesWhen: an app that was never fully closed is stuck in memory
explanation: A closed mobile app often moves to the background instead of shutting down. If it hangs there, tapping it only brings the stuck copy forward, so a force stop clears it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the banking app closes as soon as it opens
the problem began right after the app updated itself overnight
a force stop and a restart did not help
the app's stored login data is not important to keep

answer.cause: the app's cache was corrupted during the update
answer.action: Clear the app's cache from its storage settings

firstStep: Restart the device and try the app again
appliesWhen: an app stops opening right after it updates itself
explanation: Corrupted cache files are a common reason an app fails right after an update. Clearing the cache removes the bad files and does not touch most of the app's data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the scheduling app crashes now and then during the same task
the cache and the app data were already cleared
a force stop and a reboot did not stop the crashes
the user can repeat the steps that make it close

answer.cause: the app's installed files are damaged
answer.action: Back up the app's data, then uninstall and reinstall the app from the app store

appliesWhen: an app keeps crashing after the cache, data, and a reboot were tried
explanation: When the quick fixes do not stop the crashes, the installed copy itself is likely damaged. A clean reinstall from the official store replaces every file of the app.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the messaging app is several versions behind
the phone is on the office Wi-Fi every day
other apps on the phone are also out of date
a manual update from the store page works

answer.cause: automatic app updates are turned off in the app store settings
answer.action: Turn on automatic updates in the app store settings

firstStep: Try to update the app manually from the app store
appliesWhen: apps install fine but never update on their own
explanation: The app stores update apps in the background only when that setting is on. A manual update that works shows the store and the connection are fine.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the newest version of the travel app will not install
the device is about six years old
the app store says the device does not meet the requirements
plenty of free storage is available

answer.cause: the device does not meet the minimum requirements of the new app version
answer.action: Check the app's requirements and keep the current version or move to a supported device

appliesWhen: an older device no longer meets the app's minimum requirements
explanation: Developers drop older devices when new features need newer hardware or a newer OS. Check the requirements before an uninstall, because the app may not reinstall at all.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: a large game stops installing partway through
the device holds thousands of photos and videos
the Wi-Fi signal is strong
the app is listed as compatible with the device

answer.cause: the device does not have enough free storage space
answer.action: Free up space by removing unused apps and moving photos to cloud storage

firstStep: Check how much free storage space the device has
appliesWhen: the device is almost out of storage space
explanation: An app needs room for itself plus some extra free space to install. Removing unused apps and moving media off the device makes that room.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: every app is slow to respond to taps
dozens of apps and browser tabs were opened during the day
the device has not been restarted in weeks
memory use is shown near its limit

answer.cause: too many apps are running in the background and fill the RAM
answer.action: Close the unused apps and browser tabs or restart the device

appliesWhen: background apps use up the device's memory
explanation: Mobile apps go to the background instead of closing, and each one keeps its share of RAM. When RAM is full, the device swaps pages to storage and slows down.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the device became sluggish right after a major OS upgrade
the device is several years old
only a few apps are installed
storage space is not a problem

answer.cause: the new OS version needs more processing power than the old device has
answer.action: Downgrade the device to its earlier factory image

appliesWhen: an older device runs badly after it moves to a much newer OS version
explanation: Newer OS versions use more CPU resources, so an old device can run slowly after an upgrade. Going back to the original image usually needs a USB connection to a computer and a full battery.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

clues: the OS update downloads only a few percent and then stops
the user is travelling and works only on the cellular network
the device has enough free storage
the update is listed for this model

answer.cause: the OS will not download a large update over a metered connection
answer.action: Connect to a Wi-Fi network and run the update again

firstStep: Check whether the device is connected to Wi-Fi
appliesWhen: an update waits because the device uses only cellular data
explanation: Many mobile operating systems treat cellular data as metered and hold back large downloads. On a stable Wi-Fi connection the update can download and install.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: no new OS update has been offered for over a year
coworkers with newer models got the update weeks ago
the device is seven years old
a reboot and a strong Wi-Fi connection did not help

answer.cause: the vendor no longer supports the device hardware for OS updates
answer.action: Replace the device with a model that still receives updates

appliesWhen: the hardware is older than the vendor's support period
explanation: Vendors usually support a device for about five to seven years. After that the hardware is not compatible with new OS versions, so a supported device is the only way to get updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the battery is empty by early afternoon
the battery usage screen lists a navigation app at the top
the user does not remember opening that app today
the phone feels warm in the pocket

answer.cause: a power-hungry app keeps running in the background
answer.action: Close the app and limit its background activity

firstStep: Check the battery usage list for apps that use the most power
appliesWhen: one app uses much of the battery while it runs in the background
explanation: GPS apps and games use a lot of power, even when they run in the background. Closing them and limiting background activity saves battery life.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the battery drains fast only on days in the basement storeroom
the signal indicator often shows no bars there
no app shows high battery use
the battery lasts all day at home

answer.cause: the phone keeps searching for a cellular signal in a dead spot
answer.action: Turn on Airplane mode in the dead spot and turn on only the Wi-Fi that is needed

appliesWhen: the device sits in an area with no cellular signal
explanation: In a dead spot the phone keeps trying to find a signal, which drains the battery. Airplane mode turns off all radios, and the user can turn on Wi-Fi alone.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

clues: the battery no longer lasts half a day
the device gets hot while it charges
the device is four years old
the battery health screen shows a low maximum capacity

answer.cause: the battery is old and has lost much of its capacity
answer.action: Have the battery replaced by an authorized service center

appliesWhen: the battery itself is worn out from age
explanation: Lithium-ion batteries lose capacity with age and heat. When an old battery no longer holds a charge, replacing it is the fix.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the device restarts on its own several times a day
the restarts began after a free game was installed last week
the OS is up to date
the battery is healthy and charged

answer.cause: the newly installed app is unstable or not compatible with the device
answer.action: Uninstall the app that was installed just before the reboots began

firstStep: Ask the user what changed on the device just before the reboots began
appliesWhen: the reboots began right after a new app was installed
explanation: When random reboots start right after an install, that app is the most likely trigger. Removing it and watching the device confirms the cause.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the phone restarts at almost the same time each night
no apps were installed recently
the battery and storage are fine
the restarts happen while the phone is idle

answer.cause: the Auto Restart feature was turned on by mistake
answer.action: Turn off the Auto Restart setting

appliesWhen: the phone reboots on a schedule while it is idle
explanation: Some Android phones have a feature that restarts the phone on a schedule. If it was turned on by mistake, the phone seems to reboot at random.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the phone restarts during long drives on hot days
a GPS app runs the whole trip
the phone sits on the dashboard in direct sun
the phone works fine indoors

answer.cause: the phone is overheating
answer.action: Move the phone out of direct sun, remove its case, and let it cool down

appliesWhen: heat from the sun or a busy app makes the device protect itself
explanation: Mobile devices shut down or restart to protect the battery when they get too hot. Direct sun and resource-heavy apps such as GPS raise the temperature quickly.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the device has no cellular service and no Wi-Fi
the Bluetooth earbuds also stopped connecting
the user was on a flight yesterday
a coworker's device works in the same room

answer.cause: Airplane mode is still turned on
answer.action: Turn off Airplane mode

appliesWhen: every radio on the device is off at the same time
explanation: One setting turns off the cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and NFC radios together. Users often turn it on for a flight and forget it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the device no longer joins the office wireless network
the network passphrase was changed over the weekend
the device still connects to other networks
the device keeps saying it cannot join with the saved settings

answer.cause: the saved wireless profile still holds the old passphrase
answer.action: Forget the network and join it again with the new passphrase

appliesWhen: a saved network profile no longer matches the network's settings
explanation: The device tries the saved settings each time it joins. Removing the saved network and joining again stores the new passphrase.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

clues: the wireless connection drops several times an hour
the drops happen most when the break-room microwave runs
the device connects to a 2.4 GHz network
the signal is strong at the desk

answer.cause: interference on the 2.4 GHz band
answer.action: Connect the device to an SSID on the 5 GHz band

appliesWhen: other devices on the 2.4 GHz band interrupt the wireless signal
explanation: Microwave ovens and Bluetooth devices share the 2.4 GHz band and cause intermittent drops. A 5 GHz network has more channels and less of that interference.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the new headset does not show up in the device list
the smartwatch and the car stereo still connect
the headset is fully charged
the headset was just taken out of the box

answer.cause: the headset is not in pairing mode
answer.action: Put the headset in discoverable mode and pair it with the passcode from its documentation

appliesWhen: the accessory is not discoverable or the pairing code is wrong
explanation: A Bluetooth accessory must be turned on and discoverable before a device can pair with it. Some accessories also need a vendor passcode such as 0000 or 1234.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: tap-to-pay fails at every store
the payment app shows the card is valid
the user recently bought a rugged case with a metal back
other customers pay at the same reader

answer.cause: the metal-backed case blocks the NFC signal
answer.action: Remove the case and try the payment again

appliesWhen: a thick or metal case sits over the NFC antenna
explanation: NFC works only over a few centimeters and some cases block the antenna. Other customers paying at the same reader rules out the reader.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the screen stays in portrait when the device is turned sideways
videos play only in a small window
a child used the device over the weekend
the problem happens in every app

answer.cause: the orientation lock is turned on
answer.action: Turn off the orientation lock in the quick settings or Control Center

appliesWhen: the rotation lock setting holds the screen in one orientation
explanation: Users often turn on the orientation lock by accident. On iOS it is Portrait Orientation Lock in Control Center, and on Android it is the rotation setting in quick settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the screen will not turn to landscape in any app
the orientation lock is off
a reboot did not help
the device was dropped last week

answer.cause: the orientation sensor has failed
answer.action: Test the sensors and send the device to a service center if one has failed

firstStep: Reboot the device to close any app that holds the orientation
appliesWhen: the screen will not rotate after software causes were ruled out
explanation: When the lock is off and a reboot does not help, a hardware fault is likely. A sensor test app or the service center can confirm a bad sensor.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the user installed a video app from a file on a website
the phone is much slower since then
the phone asked to allow installs from unknown sources
the app asks for access to contacts and messages

answer.cause: a malicious app installed by sideloading an APK
answer.action: Uninstall the sideloaded app and scan the phone with antimalware

firstStep: Review the permissions of the newly installed app
appliesWhen: an app was installed from a file instead of the official store
explanation: Sideloaded APKs skip the checks of the official app store and may carry malware. A video app that wants contacts and messages is a red flag.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 55: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems Security Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the MDM console flags the phone as noncompliant
a computer can control the phone through its USB cable
a mock location app is selected in the settings
the user tapped the build number several times after reading a forum post

answer.cause: the hidden settings for app developers were turned on
answer.action: Turn off Developer options and USB debugging

appliesWhen: developer settings such as USB debugging or a mock location are on
explanation: Developer mode allows USB debugging, sideloading, and mock GPS locations. A mock location can trick location-based security, so it is a security concern on a work phone.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

clues: the MDM blocks company email on the phone
the phone runs a custom firmware the user flashed
the vendor's security updates no longer arrive
the hotspot feature works without a carrier plan

answer.cause: the phone has been rooted
answer.action: Restore the vendor's stock OS or replace the phone before it gets company access

appliesWhen: a user has gained super-user access to an Android phone
explanation: Rooting gives the user super-user access and often replaces the firmware, which ends vendor patches. MDM policies often block rooted devices from company data.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 55: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems Security Issues

clues: the MDM reports that the iPhone failed its integrity check
apps from an unofficial store are on the home screen
some apps are hidden from the home screen
the user wanted extra photo modes

answer.cause: the iPhone has been jailbroken
answer.action: Restore the iPhone to stock iOS and block it from company data until it is compliant

appliesWhen: a user has removed the iOS restrictions to get root-level access
explanation: Jailbreaking changes iOS to get higher access, so malware can install and hide itself. MDM attestation can reveal a jailbroken device.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 55: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems Security Issues

clues: the user installed a free copy of a paid photo editor
the copy came as an APK from a file-sharing site
the phone now uses far more data than before
the battery drains faster than usual

answer.cause: a cracked app that carries malware
answer.action: Remove the cracked app, scan the phone, and buy the app from the official store

appliesWhen: a pirated copy of a paid app was installed
explanation: A bootleg app is a paid app with its DRM removed, and it often carries malware because that pays the bootlegger. The hidden payload uses data and power.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the bank app on the phone has only a few hundred downloads
its publisher name is different from the bank's
the icon looks a little different from the bank's website
the user's bank password stopped working

answer.cause: a fake app that copies the look of a legitimate app
answer.action: Remove the app, change the bank password, and install the bank's app from its verified publisher

firstStep: Check the app's publisher name and number of downloads in the store
appliesWhen: an app pretends to be a well-known app
explanation: Spoofed apps imitate a real app to steal data. A different publisher, an odd icon, and few downloads are warning signs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 55: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems Security Issues

clues: the network traffic stays high even when the device is idle
the spikes last for hours at night
the user's habits have not changed
a new flashlight app was installed this month

answer.cause: a malicious app is sending data from the device
answer.action: Find the app that makes the traffic and uninstall it

firstStep: Close apps one at a time while you watch the network traffic
appliesWhen: an app sends data out of the device without the user's knowledge
explanation: Long traffic spikes can mean data is being stolen from or relayed through the device. When the traffic drops after an app closes, that app is the likely culprit.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the carrier sent a notice that the data limit is used up
the user's use of the phone has not changed
the battery drains quickly
the device runs warm while idle

answer.cause: the device is compromised and is used as a bot
answer.action: Take the device off the network, isolate it, and scan it for malware

appliesWhen: data use rises without any change in what the user does
explanation: Malware can use a device to send spam or attack other systems, which uses up the data plan. A usage baseline from earlier months shows that the use is abnormal.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 55: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems Security Issues

clues: web pages load only some of the time on this device
coworkers on the same network have no problems
a reboot did not help
nothing changed in the wireless network or the radio firmware

answer.cause: a malicious app is proxying or monopolizing the connection
answer.action: Run an antimalware scan and add a mobile firewall

appliesWhen: the usual network causes are ruled out and only one device has the problem
explanation: When the network, firmware, and other users are fine, malware is a likely cause. Malicious apps proxy the connection to sniff credentials, which makes it intermittent.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: a full-screen warning says the device is infected
the warning asks the user to install a cleaner app
the warning appears even when no browser is open
the device has become sluggish

answer.cause: malware is installed on the device
answer.action: Factory reset the device and install antimalware before reinstalling apps

appliesWhen: fake security warnings appear on the device
explanation: A fake security warning should be treated as a sign that malware is installed. A factory reset removes it, and antimalware should be in place before the apps return.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: ads cover the home screen several times an hour
the ads began after a few free games were installed
the ads appear even when no app is open
the device is slow to respond

answer.cause: adware came with one of the newly installed apps
answer.action: Uninstall the newly installed apps one at a time until the ads stop

appliesWhen: ads appear outside of any app after new apps were installed
explanation: A high number of ads is a sign of adware, which usually comes with a malicious app. Removing new apps one by one is quick and shows which app is to blame.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 55: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems Security Issues

clues: the user hears shutter sounds when no one is taking pictures
processor use and battery drain are high
an unknown app has permission to use the camera
the device is warm when it is not in use

answer.cause: a Trojan has taken control of the camera
answer.action: Force stop the unknown app and remove its camera permission, then scan the device

appliesWhen: an unknown app uses the camera without the user's action
explanation: High resource use and power drain can mean a Trojan is using the camera. The camera permission list shows which apps can use it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 55: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems Security Issues

clues: the computer cannot reach the file server or the intranet
popular websites open look-alike pages
the network adapter shows a good connection
the IPv4 settings list an unknown name server

answer.cause: malware changed the computer's DNS server settings
answer.action: Remove the malware and set the DNS servers back to the correct addresses

appliesWhen: name resolution goes to a server the attacker controls
explanation: Some malware changes the DNS servers, so the attacker controls where names resolve. That can block network services and redirect the browser.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: web pages load slowly in every browser
extra ads appear on trusted sites
the system proxy setting lists an unknown address
the user did not set up a proxy

answer.cause: malware set the system to use a malicious proxy
answer.action: Remove the proxy setting and scan the computer for malware

firstStep: Check the system's proxy settings
appliesWhen: web traffic goes through a proxy the user did not set
explanation: A malicious proxy sends web traffic through the attacker's server, which slows browsing and lets the attacker inject ads. Proxy settings should be checked for changes.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: a box that looks like a Windows message says a security error was found
the box shows a phone number for support
the box asks the user to call right away
the company's antivirus shows no alert

answer.cause: a fake desktop alert made to trick the user
answer.action: Do not call the number, close the alert, and run a full antimalware scan

appliesWhen: a message made to look like Windows asks the user to call a number
explanation: Fake desktop alerts copy the look of Windows to social engineer the user. The number reaches scammers who sell software the user does not need.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: a security program the company does not use says it found dozens of threats
the program asks for payment to remove them
it says the real antivirus is turned off
the program appeared after a download

answer.cause: rogue antivirus malware
answer.action: Do not interact with the program and remove it with the company's real antimalware tool

appliesWhen: an unknown security program reports threats and asks for money
explanation: Rogue antivirus software poses as a security product and reports made-up problems. Knowing which antivirus the company actually uses is the best defense.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 56: Troubleshooting PC Security Issues

clues: an email warns of a new virus that destroys hardware
the email tells the user to forward it to everyone they know
the antivirus vendor's website lists no such threat
no computer in the office shows any symptom

answer.cause: a virus hoax
answer.action: Check the warning on the CISA or antivirus vendor website and delete the email without forwarding it

appliesWhen: a warning message tells people to spread it but describes no real threat
explanation: Hoaxes spread panic through warnings that claim impossible damage. Checking a trusted source and not forwarding the email lets the hoax die out.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the user's documents all have a new file extension
the files will not open
a text file with payment instructions is in every folder
more files change while the technician watches

answer.cause: ransomware is encrypting the files
answer.action: Isolate the computer, remove the malware, and restore the files from a backup

firstStep: Disconnect the computer from the network
appliesWhen: files are renamed and locked and a payment note appears
explanation: Ransomware encrypts files, renames them with a new extension, and leaves a note in each folder. Isolating the computer stops it from reaching more files on the network.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: printing and saving fail in every program
the antimalware tool removed a rootkit yesterday
some system files have recent change dates
access denied errors appear for normal tasks

answer.cause: malware replaced or altered Windows system files
answer.action: Run System File Checker to restore the protected system files

appliesWhen: Windows system files were changed or removed by malware
explanation: Malware can delete or replace key system files, so the tasks that use them fail. System File Checker restores the trusted versions of missing or altered files.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: ads keep appearing as notifications in the corner of the screen
the notifications appear even when the browser is minimized
the user clicked Allow on a prize website last week
a malware scan finds nothing

answer.cause: the user allowed a malicious website to send push notifications
answer.action: Remove the website's permission to send notifications in the browser settings

appliesWhen: a website was allowed to send notifications to the desktop
explanation: A malicious site can coax the user into allowing push notifications and then push ads that look like OS messages. Reviewing the sites allowed to notify stops them.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the nightly update fails with the same error each time
the system drive has only a few hundred megabytes free
the internet connection works
other computers got the update

answer.cause: the system drive does not have enough free space for the update
answer.action: Free up space on the system drive and run Windows Update again

firstStep: Run the Windows Update troubleshooter and note the error code
appliesWhen: the system drive is nearly full when an update installs
explanation: An update needs free space on the system drive, or it fails. After space is freed, running Windows Update again usually installs it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 56: Troubleshooting PC Security Issues

clues: the antivirus program turns itself off
the antivirus will not update its definitions
the firewall was turned off without the user's action
new icons appeared on the desktop

answer.cause: malware is disabling the security software
answer.action: Boot into a clean environment and scan with an up-to-date antimalware tool

appliesWhen: the protection tools are turned off by something other than the user
explanation: Malware often turns off antivirus and firewall programs so it can run unseen. A scan from a clean boot environment avoids the malware that is running.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 56: Troubleshooting PC Security Issues

clues: new windows with ads open on several trusted websites
the problem is only in one browser
a full malware scan is clean
a coworker changed the browser settings to use an old web app

answer.cause: the browser's pop-up blocker was turned off
answer.action: Turn the pop-up blocker back on and allow pop-ups only for the sites that need them

appliesWhen: pop-ups appear because the browser no longer blocks them
explanation: Modern browsers block pop-ups by default and let the user allow them per site. When the blocker is off, every pop-up gets through.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 56: Troubleshooting PC Security Issues

clues: pop-ups and overlays appear on nearly every page
the pop-up blocker is on
a coupon extension was added last week
the browser has become slow

answer.cause: an adware browser extension
answer.action: Remove the extension and scan the computer with antimalware

appliesWhen: a browser add-on injects ads into web pages
explanation: Adware and malicious extensions inject pop-ups and overlays even when the blocker is on. They also use resources and slow the browser.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 56: Troubleshooting PC Security Issues

clues: every secure website shows a certificate warning
the clock in the taskbar shows a date two years ago
the warnings say the certificates are not yet valid
the computer is old and was unplugged for a month

answer.cause: the system date and time are wrong
answer.action: Correct the date and time and sync the clock with a time server

appliesWhen: the computer's clock does not match the certificates' valid dates
explanation: Browsers compare a certificate's valid dates with the computer's clock. A wrong date makes valid certificates look expired or not yet valid.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the warning appears only on the web page of a new network switch
the certificate's Issued To and Issued By fields are the same
the address bar shows Not secure
the switch was set up by the IT team

answer.cause: the device uses a self-signed certificate
answer.action: Verify the device and import its certificate into the trusted certificate store

firstStep: View the certificate details in the browser
appliesWhen: a certificate is signed by the device itself and not by a trusted CA
explanation: Network management pages often use self-signed certificates, which browsers do not trust. After the device is verified, importing its certificate stops the warning.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: typing the bank's address opens a page that looks almost the same
the problem happens only on this computer
the computer uses the same DNS servers as the others
the fake page asks for the user's login

answer.cause: the hosts file was changed to redirect the site
answer.action: Remove the bad entries from the hosts file and scan for malware

appliesWhen: only one computer is redirected while it uses the same DNS servers as the others
explanation: Pharming on one computer is often done by adding entries to the hosts file. Those entries win over DNS, so only that computer goes to the fake site.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the browser home page changed to an unknown site
searches go to a search engine the user did not choose
an unknown toolbar appeared
the user installed a free program last week

answer.cause: a browser hijacker came with the free program
answer.action: Remove the unwanted program and extension and reset the browser settings

appliesWhen: the home page and search engine change without the user's action
explanation: A changed home page or search engine is a common sign of spyware that hijacks the browser. Removing it and resetting the browser restores the settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 56: Troubleshooting PC Security Issues; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the browser makes the processor run at full use
the fan is loud even when only one page is open
the problem started after a visit to a streaming site
closing the visible tab does not help

answer.cause: a hidden pop-under page is running mining JavaScript
answer.action: Close all hidden browser windows, scan for malware, and use an ad blocker

appliesWhen: a hidden page or script uses the processor in the background
explanation: Pop-under pages open behind the main window and can run scripts that mine cryptocurrency. They use the CPU without the user's consent and slow the whole system.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

clues: the browser has become slow and some tabs freeze
about fifty tabs are open
the browser menu shows that an update is waiting
a malware scan is clean

answer.cause: too many open tabs and an update that needs a browser restart
answer.action: Close the extra tabs and restart the browser to finish its update

appliesWhen: the browser is slow from heavy use and a pending update
explanation: Not every slow browser has malware. Too many open tabs and an update waiting for a restart also slow it down.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security
